title: Family music, first lessons with Violet White and Mrs. Hooks
summary: Her father played mandolin; she played the family organ, took lessons from Violet White and Mrs. Hooks and graduated in music at about 11.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh, they say that my father played the mandolin, but he died when I was three years old, so I don't remember him. Oh, I see. And, oh, I, we had an organ in the front room, as they called it there. The left room. We had an old organ, and, oh, ever since I was large enough to reach it, I was trying to play it, so I used to have my cousin peddle it while I'd sit up on the stool and try to play, oh, such a terrible noise. So then I would pretend the windowsill was a piano in Oregon and play that. So when I started the school, my mother decided that she'd better give me music lessons. So I took lessons from a, from a, from the third grade teacher. She taught, she wasn't my third grade teacher, but she taught third grade in the public school, and she taught music also. Her name was Miss, uh, Violet White. So she started me taking lessons. And then, uh, later I took, uh, from, uh, Mrs. Hooks, there in Memphis, who had a Hooks School of Music. And, uh, when I was about 11 years old, she had a graduation exercise, and I was supposed to graduate in music, got my little diploma, and flowers, and everything.
What kind of pieces did you play?

That was mostly classical? Yeah, all classical. I never, it's strange that I never had heard any jazz while I was in Memphis. Only once. Or, a little at a time, I should say. I had a cousin that used, that had a guitar. When I was too small to, um, realize what he was playing, but he used to play the guitar, and he sang, uh, what the people, uh, from New Orleans called Buddy Bolden Blues. But at that time, he called it some, very nasty.
